question: How do they combine audio and text sequences in their RNN?

extractive_spans: combines the information from these sources using a feed-forward neural model
evidence: In this paper, we propose a novel multimodal dual recurrent encoder model that simultaneously utilizes text data, as well as audio signals, to permit the better understanding of speech data. Our model encodes the information from audio and text sequences using dual RNNs and then combines the information from these sources using a feed-forward neural model to predict the emotion class. Extensive experiments show that our proposed model outperforms other state-of-the-art methods in classifying the four emotion categories, and accuracies ranging from 68.8% to 71.8% are obtained when the model is applied to the IEMOCAP dataset. In particular, it resolves the issue in which predictions frequently incorrectly yield the neutral class, as occurs in previous models that focus on audio features.

title: Multimodal Speech Emotion Recognition Using Audio and Text
answer_short: concatenation of the vectors A and T
answer_rationale: Text 3 (page=7, section=Multimodal Dual Recurrent Encoder (MDRE)) explicitly states that the emotion class is predicted by applying the softmax function to the concatenation of the vectors A (audio encoding vector) and T (textual encoding vector). This indicates that the combination method is concatenation.
